Approach

Physics first, then CAD

Every project below follows the same loop. I reduce the problem to its governing equations before opening a model, so simulation confirms an estimate instead of replacing one.

  1. 1 · Define

    Loads and constraints

    Free-body diagrams, load cases, boundary conditions, and what failure looks like.

  2. 2 · Estimate

    Hand calculations

    Stress, heat flux, drag, or stiffness from first principles to set a target and a sanity check.

  3. 3 · Validate

    Simulate and test

    FEA, CFD, and COMSOL multiphysics, then physical testing to close the loop.

  4. 4 · Build

    Design for manufacture

    Iterate geometry for machining, composites, or additive, and ship a part that works.

Case studies

Selected work

Four projects that show the full loop, from governing physics to a built or validated result.

Case 01 · 2025 Structures · Vehicle team
SolidWorksFEATopology opt.Manufacturing

Rear Suspension, Gen 11 Vehicle

How much material can the trailing arm and brackets lose while still surviving every worst-case load?

Governing physicsσ = F/A + M·y/I n = σ_yield / σ_max
Approach

Resolved suspension load cases into forces at each pickup point, then used topology optimization to keep material only on the primary load paths. Checked the result with FEA against the same load cases before manufacturing.

Outcome
  • Designed and manufactured the full rear suspension
  • Passed all simulated load cases
  • Improved weight-to-strength ratio of trailing arm and brackets
Case 02 · 2025 Thermal · Fluids
COMSOLHeat transferLaminar flow

Immersion Cooling Simulation

How does a heated copper disk shed heat into still water by natural convection alone, and where on its surface is cooling weakest?

Governing physicsρ ≈ ρ₀[1 − β(T − T₀)] h = q″ / (T_s − T_∞)
Approach

Built a 3D model coupling Heat Transfer and Laminar Flow with gravity and Boussinesq buoyancy. Ramped the transient heat flux so the solver stayed stable through plume onset.

Outcome
  • Surface temperature, flow-field evolution, and plume structure over time
  • Spatial heat transfer coefficient maps at multiple time steps
  • Method ready to extend to inverted geometry and two-phase boiling
Case 03 · 2025 Robotics · Actuation
Actuator designMaterials testingModeling

Torsional Particle Jamming Actuator

Can a granular medium switch between compliant and stiff on command, and can its stiffness be predicted from particle size?

Governing physicsτ_max ≈ μ · P · A · r (friction at grain contacts under confining pressure)
Approach

Built and tested a torsional jamming device across particle sizes. Fit test data to a predictive stiffness model tied to how grains lock against each other.

Outcome
  • Validated the link between particle size and mechanical behavior
  • Built a predictive stiffness model
  • Proposed design changes for integration into robotic joints and grippers
Case 04 · 2024–25 Structures · Composites
Carbon fiberMachiningJoint design

Pedal Box Mount, Gen 10 Vehicle

How do you anchor high driver pedal loads into a carbon fiber structure without crushing the laminate at the bolts?

Governing physicsF_bolt,i = F·(1/N) + M·r_i / Σr_j² σ_bearing = F_bolt / (d·t)
Approach

Treated the mount as a bolt group, distributing pedal force and moment across fasteners so no single hole carries the peak load. Held tight tolerances with precision machining.

Outcome
  • Designed and manufactured a reinforced mount
  • Optimized fastener load distribution in the composite
  • Increased structural reliability of the pedal box
